newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to nominate Gordon as CIA deputy director.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to nominate Gordon as CIA deputy director.

text.p: President Clinton will nominate Air Force Lt. Gen. John Gordon as deputy director of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), the White House said Monday.

Gordon, currently associate director for military support at the CIA, previously worked on defence and arms control issues at the National Security Council and served as director of operations for the Air Force Space Command.
His appointment is subject to Senate confirmation.
CIA Director George Tenet lauded Clinton's decision to nominate Gordon and said his broad background made him "superbly qualified" for the No. 2 job at the spy agency.

Gordon, in a statement released by the CIA, said he was honoured by Clinton's intention to nominate him and looked forward to the challenges of addressing "current and future intelligence challenges."

Tenet, vowing to make the CIA the "world's best espionage organisation," also announced nine other members of his management team, including David Carey as executive director, Regina Genton as deputy executive director, Jack Downing as deputy director for operations and James Pavitt as associate deputy director for operations.

Other nominees included John Gannon as chairman of the National Intelligence Council, Ellen Laipson as vice chairman for estimates at the council, John McLaughlin as CIA deputy director for intelligence, Winston Wiley as associate deputy director for intelligence and Joan Dempsey as chief of staff to Tenet.

"Our mission is clear," Tenet said in announcing the appointments. "At the end of the day, it is our job to ensure that our nation's leaders have the information and time they need to avert danger to the United States and, when it cannot be averted, the wherewithal to prevail."
